QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_41

question.text: The fundamental intuition behind the Public Market Equivalent (PME) method as used in KS-PME is:

answer.text: PME compounds capital calls and distributions using the public index return to construct a counterfactual 'what-if-invested-in-index' baseline; KS-PME > 1 means the AIF outperformed the public market.
PME is the 5-year trailing CAGR of the broadest index in the AIF's country of domicile.
PME is the geometric mean of all listed-peer companies' returns minus risk-free.
PME is the quarterly change in NAV times the AIF's beta.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.3.5: KS-PME measures the relative efficiency of Cat I/II AIF investments vis-à-vis listed-market index returns. It compounds capital calls and distributions at the market rate to the valuation date and computes the resulting TVPI. KS-PME > 1 = outperformance; < 1 = underperformance. The Trap: B is just CAGR, not PME. C describes peer-alpha, not PME. D is CAPM-style beta mechanics, not PME. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests PME rationale. Cambridge, PitchBook, Preqin all report KS-PME for PE/VC funds globally. Manager's Pro-Tip: LP due-diligence teams (especially foreign pension funds) ALWAYS compute KS-PME themselves against S&P 500 or MSCI India. Pre-empt by providing KS-PME vs TWO indices (domestic + global) in your fundraising deck.
